Name: Trisha Voellinger
Badge: Reading to Write: They Say / I Say
Which version of the They Say / I Say routine (with visual texts or with annotation) feels like the best fit for your students right now? Why?:

The They Say/I Say routine with visual texts feels like the best fit for students right now because we are just getting started on writing strategies. A majority of the students are struggling finding their voice and putting their words on paper. I feel like the visuals is a low stake start for gaining a foundation for their writing skills.

Describe one way you might adapt the They Say / I Say framework to align with the types of texts your students read most often (e.g., articles, visuals, multimodal texts).:

One way I might adapt the They Say/I Say framework to align with science texts is by using visuals, such as photographs, graphs, or infographics, before, during, and after a topic. This would be a great way to introduce, expand, and reflect on information we are learning. After the class gets used to the procedure, I can find articles related to my science topics for annotatations. I believe this would be beneficial for them to comprehend and expand their knowledge for the topic.

What, if anything, do you need help thinking through as you plan for using They Say / I Say in your classroom?:

I would need help with transitioning over to annotations from visuals. I will have to some planning, and I will need to guide the students on the transition.
